correctness.rationale: The binary suffix language tiles by 1 and 00. For suffix length l>=2 the initial 00 and 1 blocks are ordered, have sizes F_(l-1) and F_l, and meet at a unique gap 2^(l-2)+1+min(T_(l-1)). Minima alternate 0 and 1; maxima are 2^l-1. A bridge first made at length j is inherited in F_(l-j+1) copies, including the base l=j. Summing over the positive shells reproduces F_(N-j+2)-1. There are N shell boundaries including 0 to 1, with alternating gaps 1,2 starting at 1. This checks N=1,2 and the coincidence j=2,3. The limiting atoms from Binet sum to one (so no mass escapes), their geometric tail has the claimed value, and the mean series diverges since 2/phi>1. The finite mean follows directly by telescoping from 0 to 2^N-1. A separately written trailing-digit recurrence checks every dyadic cutoff N=1..20; it is corroboration, not the infinite proof.
residual_risks: The audited theorem concerns dyadic windows only, not arbitrary cutoffs.
